hard_gates.gate: G2 permissions on the real product: a role held only in company X must grant nothing on company Y's records
hard_gates.evidence: attack/cross-company-role.log, attack/cross-company-more.log, attack/cross-company-audit.txt, shot 01. In the seeded demo, accountant@alnoor.example holds 'Company manager' (tenancy.companies.update, branches.create/update) only in ALN-DXB and 'Read-only' in ALN-FZE. While working in FZE, PUT /companies/{FZE} and PUT /branches/{FZE branch} answer 403, which is correct. After switching to DXB, the same user's PUT /api/tenancy/companies/{FZE id} answers 200: the trade licence changed from JAFZA-178204 to X-ALN-DXB-6395. PUT /api/tenancy/branches/{JAFZA-WH} answers 200 (city changed). POST /api/tenancy/branches {companyId: FZE} answers 201 (branch SIDE created in FZE). Audit rows 202124 and 202125 name the accountant. The screen agrees with the API: the FZE company form opens editable with Save while the user works in DXB (shot 01). The session's permissions are the working company's grants, while the company scope (RLS) is every company the user works in. No endpoint checks the permission in the record's own company, so 'every action is denied unless a role grants it' is broken on this piece's endpoints. G2CompanyRoleTests only checks a user who is working in Y, never a user working in X who names Y's record, so the whole gate suite passes.

biggest_gap.title: A role held in one company acts on another company's records: Company manager in ALN-DXB, Read-only in ALN-FZE, changes FZE's company and branches and creates FZE branches while working in DXB
biggest_gap.detail: Permissions for a request are the workspace roles plus the roles of the working company. The company scope that RLS enforces is every company the user works in. No tenancy endpoint (companies update and logo, branches create and update, and access update too) checks the permission in the company of the record it touches, and the kernel's SaveChanges guard checks only that the company is in scope. So a group's 'accountant in the Dubai LLC, read-only in the JAFZA entity' (the case per-company roles were built for) can rewrite the JAFZA entity's legal registration (trade licence, TRN, the Arabic-legal-name setting, active flag), its branches, and create new branches in it. Switching to the company where they hold the role is all it takes. The screen offers it too: the FZE form opens with Save while the user works in DXB. G2CompanyRoleTests checks only a user who is working in Y, so every gate passes. Fix: authorise company-owned writes and reads against the grants held in the record's own company, for example a kernel check that every ICompanyOwned row written in a request lies in a company where the declared permission is covered (UserGrants.Covers(permission, companyId)), or narrow the session's write scope to the companies where the permission is held. Add the gate: for every endpoint and permission held only in X, a user working in X who names Y's records (path ids, body companyId) gets 403 and changes nothing. Plant 'permission checked in the working company only' in the gate self-tests. The screens should also offer edit only where the role is held.
biggest_gap.evidence: Run ERP_PROJECT=x ERP_HTTP_PORT=20250 ERP_DB_PORT=20251 ./erp up, then node attack/cross-company-role.mjs http://localhost:20250 and node attack/cross-company-more.mjs. Results (cross-company-role.log): working in ALN-FZE, PUT branch and PUT company give 403. After switching to ALN-DXB, PUT /api/tenancy/branches/{JAFZA-WH} gives 200 and PUT /api/tenancy/companies/{ALN-FZE} gives 200 (tradeLicenceNumber JAFZA-178204 -> X-ALN-DXB-6395). Then POST /api/tenancy/branches {companyId: ALN-FZE} gives 201 (code SIDE). Audit rows 202124 and 202125 name accountant@alnoor.example (attack/cross-company-audit.txt). Shot 01 shows the FZE form editable with Save while the user works in DXB. The unplanted ./erp verify passed (1665/1665), so no gate catches it.

other_findings: The write-set gate (G2WriteSetTests, new this round) misses a side door that writes a value equal to the stored one. Plant P1d makes the workplace switch also set the company's fiscalYearStartMonth, validated to 1 to 12, only for a whole-workspace holder. The gate sends 1 to companies already at 1, so the audit trail records no change and the test passed. The suite still failed, but only through G1BranchScopeAttackTests, whose message ('answered 200, expected a refusal') suggests it judges the accepted request, not the write. Suggestion: for every field that is not the record's own, send a value that differs from what is stored (read the record first, or send two different values), then compare the audit trail. Evidence: plant-P1d.diff, P1d-gates.log.
Round 10 gap closed: the round 10 P1b plant (the workplace switch sets arabicLegalNameRequired) is now caught by G2WriteSetTests (batchA-gates.log).

In plant runs P1c and A, G1HttpIsolationTests also failed, but only through server errors (500) that the plant itself caused: a fiscal-month CHECK violation, or DateTime.DaysInMonth(0). This is an accidental catch, not a judgment of what was written.

The English legal name accepts Arabic script. In the Arabic walk, typing Arabic into the English legal name field saved company '60473' with legal name (English) 'فرع ديرة 60473' and a numeric-only code (ui/walk3.log, shot 06). UAE trade licences carry a Latin-script English name; consider refusing or warning when the English field has no Latin letters.
In the Arabic walk, after a branch was added to the new company TEST from its form, the companies list still showed 0 branches for TEST until refreshed (shot 06). I did not recheck it after a reload.

Arabic keyboard path: Alt+N focuses the Arabic legal name, Tab goes to the English legal name, and Ctrl+S moves the focus to the branch line, which is prefilled with '<company> - ' in both languages. A branch saved with only an Arabic name is announced as having no English name (shot 04). The switcher opens on Alt+C and filters by typing (shots 05 and 06).
